bills.title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026
bills.official_title: To authorize appropriations for fiscal year 2026 for military activities of the Department of Defense, for military construction, and for defense activities of the Department of Energy, to prescribe military personnel strengths for such fiscal year, and for other purposes.
bills.summary: This is the Senate's own version of the annual defense authorization bill for fiscal year 2026 — the Armed Services Committee's original measure, reported by Senator Wicker with written report No. 119-39. It runs to ten divisions: Department of Defense authorizations, military construction, Department of Energy nuclear-security programs, the funding tables that give the authorizations their dollar amounts, an additional-provisions division, and five more divisions carrying an intelligence authorization, State Department matters, a State Department authorization act, a Coast Guard authorization act, and a full housing package. It is a different vehicle from the fiscal year 2026 defense authorization that became law: that was S. 1071, enacted as Public Law 119-60 on December 18, 2025.
bills.brief: The Senate Armed Services Committee's fiscal year 2026 defense authorization vehicle — ten divisions covering Defense, military construction, Energy nuclear programs, intelligence, the State Department, the Coast Guard, and a housing title.

bills.likelihoodReason: This is a committee-originated measure with no cosponsors, which is normal for an Armed Services original measure and says nothing about its support. The decisive structural fact is that a fiscal year 2026 defense authorization has already been enacted under a different bill number, S. 1071, so the fiscal year this text authorizes is already covered by law and there is no remaining legislative need for this vehicle. Individual divisions carried here — the Coast Guard authorization, the ROAD to Housing package, the Development Finance Corporation reauthorization — remain plausible candidates to move attached to other vehicles, but that would be a different bill.

sections.label: Division A — Department of Defense Authorizations

items.main: Sets active-duty end strengths as of September 30, 2026 at 454,000 Army, 344,600 Navy, 172,300 Marine Corps, 321,500 Air Force, and 10,400 Space Force.
items.detail: Selected Reserve strengths are set at 328,000 Army National Guard, 172,000 Army Reserve, 57,500 Navy Reserve, 33,600 Marine Corps Reserve, 106,300 Air National Guard, 67,500 Air Force Reserve, and 7,000 Coast Guard Reserve, with proportional reductions for units called to active duty and increases when they are released. Reserves on full-time active duty in support of the reserves are set separately, from 30,845 for the Army National Guard down to 2,400 for the Marine Corps Reserve, and minimum dual-status military technician levels are set for the Army and Air Force reserve components.

items.main: Authorizes fiscal year 2026 appropriations for procurement, research and development, operation and maintenance, and military personnel, with every dollar amount set out in the Division D funding tables rather than in the authorizing sections themselves.
items.detail: Sections 101, 201, and 301 each authorize appropriations as specified in the funding tables at sections 4101, 4201, and 4301. Division A also carries the policy provisions: limits and reporting requirements on Navy medium and large unmanned surface vessels and on the amphibious warfare ship requirement; funding prohibitions that bar reducing A-10 inventory below 103 and E-3 airborne warning and control inventory below 16, each with a certification or plan exception, plus an extension of the prohibition on certain reductions to B-1 bomber squadrons; a Biotechnology Management Office and departmental biotechnology strategy; and repeals of the prohibition on Department of Defense procurement of items containing perfluorooctane sulfonate or perfluorooctanoic acid and of the temporary moratorium on incinerating perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances.

sections.label: Division C — Department of Energy National Security Authorizations

items.main: Rewrites the statutory plutonium pit production schedule so the nuclear security enterprise must produce no fewer than 10 war reserve pits during 2025, 20 during 2026, 30 during 2027, 50 during 2029, and 80 during 2032 and later years.
items.detail: The existing schedule in section 4219 of the Atomic Energy Defense Act required 10 pits during 2024, 20 during 2025, 30 during 2026, and 80 during 2030, so each early milestone moves back a year, the 80-per-year rate moves from 2030 to 2032, and a new 50-pit milestone is inserted at 2029; the Secretary of Energy's annual certification duty is extended from 2030 to 2032 to match. Once the 80-per-year rate applies, no fewer than 30 pits a year must come from Los Alamos National Laboratory and no fewer than 50 from the Savannah River Plutonium Processing Facility in Aiken, South Carolina. The division also authorizes new National Nuclear Security Administration plant projects — $52.2M for combined radiation environments for survivability testing and $40M for a photolithography capability at Sandia National Laboratories, $26M for an enhanced fusion yield capability and $15M for product realization infrastructure for stockpile modernization at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, $20M for a modernization project at Los Alamos National Laboratory, and $75M for an East Side Office Building.

items.main: Repeals the Caesar Syria Civilian Protection Act of 2019 and replaces it with a certification report on the Government of Syria due within 90 days of enactment and every 180 days for the following 4 years.
items.detail: The report must certify whether the Government of Syria has committed to eliminating the threat from ISIS and other terrorist groups and joined the Global Coalition To Defeat ISIS, is making progress on security for and representation of religious and ethnic minorities, is refraining from unilateral unprovoked military action against neighbors including Israel, is not financing, assisting, or harboring individuals or groups harmful to U.S. national security, and has taken steps to remove foreign fighters from senior government and security roles.

items.main: Raises the Development Finance Corporation's maximum contingent liability outstanding at any one time from $60B to $200B in the aggregate, and authorizes $3B for its Equity Investment Account for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
items.detail: The contingent liability figure is a ceiling on the Corporation's outstanding exposure, not an appropriation, and the replacement text applies it to all extensions of liability regardless of the authority cited. The Equity Investment Account authorization is accompanied by a requirement to collect data on the use of the account to inform the Corporation's record of returns and its reevaluation of equity investment subsidy rates.

items.main: Adds a new advanced integrated circuit export control section to the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 and extends the Defense Production Act's section 717(a) sunset from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2026.
items.detail: The new section requires a Commerce license for the export, reexport, or in-country transfer of an advanced integrated circuit or a product containing one, except to countries listed in Country Group A:4, A:5, or A:6 of the Export Administration Regulations. For a country of concern or a country under a comprehensive U.S. arms embargo, the license applicant must certify that U.S. persons had a right of first refusal — public notice of the intent to sell, the price and quantity, and not less than 15 business days for U.S. persons to request the same terms.

sections.label: Division I — ROAD to Housing Act

items.main: Carries a full housing package inside the defense authorization, running eight titles from financial literacy and housing supply through manufactured housing, homeownership access, program reform, veterans housing, oversight, and interagency coordination.
items.detail: Title II alone contains the Housing Supply Frameworks Act, Whole-Home Repairs Act, Community Investment and Prosperity Act, Build Now Act, BUILD Housing Act, Unlocking Housing Supply Through Streamlined and Modernized Reviews Act, an Innovation Fund, the Accelerating Home Building Act, Build More Housing Near Transit Act, RESIDE Act, and Housing Affordability Act. Later titles carry the Reforming Disaster Recovery Act, a HOME Investment Partnerships reauthorization, a Rural Housing Service Reform Act, a new Moving to Work cohort, the Choice in Affordable Housing Act, and the VA Home Loan Awareness and VALID Acts.

underreported.section: Division E, Section 6211 — Repeal of Caesar Syria Civilian Protection Act of 2019
underreported.summary: A defense authorization bill repeals a standing sanctions statute outright, substituting a recurring certification report on the Government of Syria for the sanctions regime the repealed Act carried.
underreported.why_unreported: The provision sits in the additional-provisions division under a subtitle on matters relating to Syria, Iraq, and Iran, and its operative effect is the removal of an existing Act rather than a defense authorization.

underreported.section: Division E, Section 1292 — Maximum Contingent Liability
underreported.summary: The Development Finance Corporation's aggregate ceiling on outstanding contingent liability more than triples, from $60B to $200B, and the replacement text extends the ceiling to every extension of liability regardless of the authority cited.
underreported.why_unreported: The figure is a lending-exposure ceiling rather than money appropriated, so it does not appear in the funding tables that carry the bill's authorization amounts.

underreported.section: Division I — ROAD to Housing Act
underreported.summary: An entire domestic housing package — twenty-plus named Acts spanning housing supply, manufactured housing, rental assistance, disaster recovery, rural housing, and appraisal reform — travels as a division of the defense authorization bill.
underreported.why_unreported: The division's subject matter has no defense nexus, and it is one of five non-defense divisions in a bill whose stated purpose is authorizing appropriations for military activities.

underreported.section: Division A, Sections 318 and 319 — Perfluoroalkyl Substances
underreported.summary: Two sections repeal existing restrictions: the prohibition on Department of Defense procurement of items containing perfluorooctane sulfonate or perfluorooctanoic acid, and the temporary moratorium on the Department's incineration of perfluoroalkyl substances, polyfluoroalkyl substances, and aqueous film forming foam.
underreported.why_unreported: They sit in the same energy-and-environment subtitle as provisions expanding responses to perfluoroalkyl contamination, including bottled water for affected communities and interim response authority.

gaps: The bill authorizes procurement, research and development, operation and maintenance, and military personnel appropriations by cross-reference to the Division D funding tables, so the authorizing sections themselves state no dollar amount and the totals cannot be read from the operative text.

Division F authorizes appropriations for intelligence and intelligence-related activities but specifies the amounts only in a classified Schedule of Authorizations, so no intelligence authorization figure appears in the public text.

Section 6211 repeals the Caesar Syria Civilian Protection Act of 2019 and requires recurring certification reports on the Government of Syria, but attaches no consequence to a negative certification and provides no mechanism to restore the repealed authorities.

The bill is organized into ten divisions covering intelligence, State Department, Coast Guard, and housing matters alongside defense, but its stated purpose is limited to authorizing appropriations for military activities, military construction, and Department of Energy defense activities and prescribing military personnel strengths.

Section 3112 sets site-specific production floors of 30 pits a year at Los Alamos and 50 at the Savannah River Plutonium Processing Facility, but attaches them only to the 80-per-year rate required from 2032 onward, leaving the 2025 through 2029 milestones with no site allocation.

added: Active-duty and Selected Reserve end strengths for fiscal year 2026, including 454,000 Army, 344,600 Navy, 172,300 Marine Corps, 321,500 Air Force, and 10,400 Space Force

A new advanced integrated circuit export control section in the Export Control Reform Act of 2018, requiring a Commerce license outside Country Groups A:4, A:5, and A:6 and a U.S.-person right-of-first-refusal certification with not less than 15 business days notice
A recurring certification report on the Government of Syria, due within 90 days of enactment and every 180 days for the following 4 years
New National Nuclear Security Administration plant projects, including $52.2M for combined radiation environments for survivability testing and $75M for an East Side Office Building
$3B for the Development Finance Corporation Equity Investment Account for fiscal years 2026 through 2030
A Biotechnology Management Office and a Department of Defense biotechnology strategy
modified: The plutonium pit production schedule moves to no fewer than 10 pits in 2025, 20 in 2026, 30 in 2027, 50 in 2029, and 80 in 2032 and later years, with the Secretary of Energy's annual certification requirement extended from 2030 to 2032 to match
The Development Finance Corporation's maximum aggregate contingent liability outstanding at any one time rises to $200B

Coast Guard authorizations are reset to $11.85B for operation and maintenance and $3.65B for procurement, construction, renovation, and improvement in fiscal year 2026, and average military training student loads rise to 3,000 student years for recruit and special training, 200 for flight training, 450 for professional training, and 1,300 for officer acquisition
The Defense Production Act section 717(a) sunset moves from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2026
The North Atlantic Treaty Organization Security Investment Program receives $531.8M for the U.S. share of authorized projects
removed: The Caesar Syria Civilian Protection Act of 2019 is repealed
The prohibition on Department of Defense procurement of certain items containing perfluorooctane sulfonate or perfluorooctanoic acid
The temporary moratorium on Department of Defense incineration of perfluoroalkyl substances, polyfluoroalkyl substances, and aqueous film forming foam
